Morning, Paula. I have the two quotes for Santos open here. Which one do we recommend?
Option B is cheaper. It is fifty thousand reais cheaper than Option A.
So Option B is the best choice for the client.
No. Option B is cheaper, but Option A is safer for this client.
Safer. Tell me why.
The coverage in Option A is more complete: fire, flood and transport. Option B covers fire only.
And after the fire in warehouse 4, fire is not the only risk in Santos.
Exactly. And the discount for the new alarm is bigger in Option A: twelve percent.
What about the claim service? That is the worst part of the other insurer.
Option A answers a claim in twenty-four hours. Option B takes five days.
The client wants the cheapest one. What do you tell him on Thursday?
The truth. The cheapest option is not always the best one.

Hi, Paula. David here. Today I want to tell you about the worst recommendation I ever made, and it took me eight months to find out that it was bad. A client asked me for the cheapest quote. That was all he said: give me the cheapest one. So I sent him the cheapest one. I did not write a comment, I did not compare anything, I just sent the number. It was cheaper, and I was fast, and I was proud of that. Eight months later a truck with his goods was stolen on the road, and he called me. The cheap policy covered fire only. It did not cover transport. And he said something to me on the phone that I still hear today. He said: you knew, and you did not tell me. Now listen, because this is the whole lesson. Cheaper is a number. The spreadsheet says it, and anybody can read it. Better is a judgement, and the spreadsheet cannot make it. You can. And when you say it out loud, in one sentence, that is the moment you stop sending prices and start being a broker. See you soon.

Good morning, Paula. Sofia here, with the Miami trip in front of me. There are two flights on Thursday. The night flight is cheaper, nine hundred reais cheaper, and I know that looks good on the budget. But it arrives at two in the morning and your first meeting is at nine, so please think about that before you choose. The hotels are the same story. The cheaper one is forty minutes from the client's office. The other one is more expensive, but it is five minutes away, so your day is calmer and safer, and you arrive at the meeting fresh. Now the important part, and this is why I am calling. In November you will present the Santos renewal to the team in Miami. In English. Alone. I want the two options side by side, and I want your recommendation in one sentence at the end. Not a list of prices, Paula. A recommendation. And one more thing. In January you told me you were not ready to speak in a meeting. You were wrong then, and you are ready now. See you Thursday.
